The Corporation for Public Broadcasting — which helped fund NPR, PBS and many local radio and TV stations – voted to dissolve the private, nonprofit corporation after 58 years of service.

For more than half a century, it ensured that all Americans — regardless of their zip code, income, or background — had access to trusted news, educational programming.

**It’s absolutely critical that Americans continue putting pressure on Congress until the midterms to ensure public media survives through the end of the year.**

That’s why it’s so vital that we conduct our own polling, especially when there’s a discrepancy with the numbers like what we’re seeing right now. On one hand, polling shows voters prefer Republicans over Democrats on nearly every key issue: National Security: Immigration: Foreign policy: Trade: National debt: But at the same time, polling by the mainstream media shows Democrats have surged out to a whopping on the generic ballot for the midterms. body:
This isn’t about protecting our democracy, and they know it.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260220-5931-footer&t=1&akid=5931%2E420207%2Evm3wx4)
Peter,
This week, Senate Republicans are trying to push the SAVE Act forward. They claim it is about election security, but the truth is our elections are already safe and secure, and **this bill is clearly about voter suppression.**
I proudly voted **NO** on the SAVE Act in the House because it would disenfranchise millions of eligible voters by requiring a passport or birth certificate in person just to register or update your registration.
Only about half of U.S. citizens have a passport. And there are nearly _70 million married women_ who may not be able to present a valid birth certificate because they changed their name. The bill would also eliminate online voter registration across the country.
That is not protecting democracy, Peter. It’s about the GOP handpicking their voters. And it’s critical that we continue standing up against their authoritarian tactics.
[**If you are with me, please rush $3 or whatever you can to help us fight back against this authoritarian scheme and defend our right to vote.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260220.GX3Qzn&refcode=em20260220-5931&amount=3&t=2&akid=5931%2E420207%2Evm3wx4)

subject: In case you missed it…

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In case you missed it, we just unleashed our full slate of 2026 Justice
Democrats candidates running in Democratic primary races across eight
states.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260220.amFJJu&refcode=em20260220-37484&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37484%2E1203867%2EKjTSxv ]A post on X from ABC News Politics (@ABCPolitics) reading: 'Justice
Democrats, a progressive group that recruits and backs candidates in
Democratic primaries, has announced a dozen contenders for the 2026
cycle.' It includes a link to an article titled 'Progressive group rolls
out 2026 candidates, pitching working-class challengers' with a picture of
Cori Bush.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260220.amFJJu&refcode=em20260220-37484&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37484%2E1203867%2EKjTSxv ]Before I say more about what this moment means for us, consider
chipping in $5 or $10 to directly support our upcoming primary fights
here.

In this year’s midterm elections, JD is going big and swinging for the
fences by fighting to elect 12 new progressive leaders to join our bloc.

Why? Because we’re tired of the status quo, and so is the majority of
Democratic voters all over our country.

This slate is our vision to build a team of fighters in Washington that
delivers on our core mission: to build power for the working class in
Congress.

It reflects the growing movement of people who are sick of a Democratic
Party overrun by corporate PACs, billionaire-backed lobbies, and the weak
politicians they buy.

It is clear that it is not just about electing the right people — it’s
also about how they use their power once elected. We have a huge
opportunity this cycle to transform the Party through primaries at a time
when too many Do-Nothing Democrats in Congress fail to stand up to fascism
and the corporate takeover of our country.

Our communities don’t need incumbents struggling to do the bare minimum
while being propped up by the same corporate interests that exploit us.
They need leaders fighting like hell to deliver us the whole damn pie —
every member of our slate is ready to do just that.

All twelve of our endorsements refuse corporate PAC money, reject AIPAC,
and support the long-overdue policies people demand, like abolishing ICE,
passing Medicare for All and a living minimum wage, and ending U.S.
military support for Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

This is an absolutely major moment for our movement, and the opportunity
to more than DOUBLE our bloc in the halls of power. We’re bringing not
just a blue wave to the polls in 2026, but an undeniably progressive,
working-class wave.

It all starts in North Carolina and Texas on Tuesday, March 3rd, which is
just 11 days from now. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260220.amFJJu&refcode=em20260220-37484&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37484%2E1203867%2EKjTSxv ]Please,
Peter, pitch in whatever you can to fuel our
work to elect Nida Allam, Rev. Frederick Haynes, and the rest of our
slate.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260220.amFJJu&refcode=em20260220-37484&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37484%2E1203867%2EKjTSxv ]Contribute $5

Thank you for standing with us. Now, let’s go win some primaries!

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

name: Cori Bush
subject: This month, I’ve been reflecting on who carried us
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Cori For Us
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q1?refcode=x_260220_bhmstories_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q1?refcode=x_260220_bhmstories_act]
Peter,
This Black History Month, I’ve been doing a lot of reflecting.
I’ve been thinking about the Black leaders, elders, and every day people whose courage and sacrifice made it possible for me to be here, to raise my voice, to fight back, and to refuse to be silenced. I’ve been honoring the stories and the voices that have resonated deeply with me, the ones that remind me who we are and where we come from.
Because Black history is American history. And no matter how hard they try, they can’t erase us. They can’t silence us. And they sure as hell can’t stop us.
Our people have always led movements for freedom, dignity, and justice, often without credit, often at great personal cost. And still, we rise.
Now I’d love to hear from you.
Who is a Black leader or champion, past or present, who inspires you? Maybe it’s a historic figure. Maybe it’s someone close to home whose name deserves to be lifted up. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LiUKdGDd8UOPy_lMrLHL1w2]
CELEBRATING BLACK LEADERS [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LiUKdGDd8UOPy_lMrLHL1w2]
Click here to fill out our short survey and share who inspires you. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/LiUKdGDd8UOPy_lMrLHL1w2]
All month long—and every month—I’m honoring Black excellence, lifting up these stories, and making sure the sacrifices of those who came before us were not in vain. I hope you’ll join me.
And remember: history remembers the fighters.
Let’s keep fighting, together.
With love and solidarity,
Cori Bush

As a Congresswoman, she has always shown up when it’s hardest: securing disaster relief, lowering insulin costs, and delivering millions for our communities.

SCOTUS Nukes Trump's Tariffs

The Supreme Court [struck down](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOhCAYhJ8GOwz-Iq4FxTV2e-2V5l_A3T-HQAD1Hv_i5p7gkimmmZl883Vf7kiewvMTN6fNQYuNdil7ym5zJu65hv3blZr3LZWKCwhQXAAHsQS_dI3VxqoeGqe7cewUDGIam5d-oOjFY5zsBB3epEFY1XozKK14rKqTDemrSQBcksPQDoCd7KXqrUElpoFJsSeL1ZXWxFBcPrDS4SiEeLkYWhO3xutXramw_oPBzGA-z7Nd409w5xXbGMwpeqpkCoP5j4q_sbh1hgrFwG0M6C1_I_KKmdaVp3i6XJqsbTrJeypqZFI8NyT_3q3_uOrQ8BsAAP__8M98HQ) President Trump's sweeping global tariffs Friday in a 6-3 ruling. Chief Justice Roberts held that IEEPA -- the 1977 emergency law Trump used to impose reciprocal tariffs -- does not authorize import taxes. The ruling does not kill all of Trump's tariffs; Section 232 and other statutes remain intact. Justices Thomas, Alito, and Kavanaugh [dissented](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLFu7CAQRb8Gd6zw2MC6oHiNu31tSmsEs7ujYLAAO78f2ckXRJriSiPdo3M_HssDOXJ6_ceVnD94CTksdd8KreTzXlraP6m2sq9bbbiAAiMVSFBLikvfBeeDGaAj11vbG9Bqst3b2UmFuzYaCRX2zwl7e6fJ2kFp7w3pjt3ZpADOG7W-acB-HEYzBI9GTVqMat8CNqo3n1OlcmDjgzilfKacbj6vXXTv1rYqhn8CZgFzyTF6jPF8CphPhoBZwZUFzL9i8jKTnA6MfEHkj6FsWPj5lIVevJKAuSsubF8cI1djxaheK_LV3rU_rHU4-A4AAP__Jjh5UQ), with Kavanaugh warning of a "mess" in refunding over $130 billion already collected. Trump, informed mid-meeting with governors, called the ruling [a "disgrace"](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDFuxCAQRU-DOywYMOwWFGncbdqUFgvjNQoGC7Ct3D7yKieINMWTRvpf7389pocNMaTXp13RuCNMPvup7lvBFV3eS0v7N9ZW9nWrzU7AQFEGFNiU4sQ7b5xXAjo0XGuuYGB33S0GnzchFXNcM8UHeAqv59uM3AnhZzGrLpgriQFcJ4ehH8ByKaQS3lnF7gORbN-8bVh7l1PFctgWDgwp5Yty6l1eu2iW1rZKxAeBkcB4nmf_Y5ecry-BMeFZCYy2tOAiXvg2oc7GWOmfJn170mZLmGfKFROcayX7pa2xK8ZvZ4gxVKWJZK_Vhviubv9Y6zDwGwAA__8KrXpc) and said he has a backup plan. A press conference followed at 12:45 p.m. ★★★
Trump Eyes Iran Strike

President Trump confirmed Friday morning he is [actively considering](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2OqzAUhJ8GOiPbGBMKF7ehy223RGftQ3IU_yDbwObtV-QRVppimvk0M1_35Q7kKT7-Q0BjD1pcckvZt4wBbdpzjfsLS8172EqFRXKpGZdM8iX6RbTOWKd72aIR4yi0HPg0tk-DSqywipualBphcKKf1ptAxUXf6-9Rt2QuEpfykhqGbpAgVK907yxoPg2N4vvmoGLpbIoF8wGVDqQY0-VS7GwKrTfPWrfS9P8aOTdyPs-zW9NPxPOKhUbOW_JUyZZGzp8RrMC7sCeyi0oOM8UH8xSoomOBPFXIb1ZqpheyLWMpe0ZGGSKLu_UImTkE32bjtpO8p6LHRvFHAPKfSvUPLx5G_gYAAP__4SCFlA) a limited military strike on Iran -- the clearest signal yet that diplomacy is running out of runway. "I guess I can say I am considering it," Trump told reporters at the White House. Two carrier groups are now in the region. The USS Abraham Lincoln is already deployed in the Arabian Sea; the USS Gerald R. Ford is en route. Trump has given Tehran a 15-day deadline, and Iran held military drills with Russia on Thursday as [the second carrier drew closer](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDHO4yAQRk-DOyw8NjgpKLZxl223tCZAklEwtgaw9_gr9gi_NMUnPenpaf481gdSpPT-jVuw7qTV737N9eCwBbdXLql-Qy5ctyMXXEGBkQokqDXFdei8dd6M0AU7zPNgQKv73H0svEbz1AjmBei1988bajU7Y54wq3DTHdlmUgDtJq17DThM42RG79CouxaTqofHEnLv9pQDn1joDJTS3taeerdvXbSfUo4sxl8CFgHLdV19Clfe8G_jApZjj1TIZQELMSZZs-SaM6H0TDHKVF0MyLJg_GaJxI7xVaRDZgosYGmdAhYFApbh3jS-LZjMPDXQsfXHRTFSNrOY1HtDiv_jyg_-eVr4FwAA__-WsoPX). Tehran is [fortifying nuclear sites](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL1uhTAMhZ8mbKBgknAZMnTJdrt2RL6JC1Hzg0iA16-4fYNKHrzY3_nO13N-og8-LZ8YSdvTzy67uRzbTpFsPvaajh8qdT_iVirOwEG1HFrgcwpz3zhtnRqgId2PY69A8mlsVq2A-vGl5EM4Mb2ERGWlJC5Gko74QzRe3584wD1Cyk4C9mIQanAWFZ8kE_zYHFYqnc2p0H5i9Sf5lPK95dTZHJug11q3woYPBoaBua6ru7CsPi01p-rj-zwyMImuwsDcVAbmm14MTD8xMH9qrd8xtXbFECgt1DrC0Lq3uL1pDEyza7ddPgRf1MgEXyL68E5R_1HcqeE3AAD__8cxfaE) with concrete and soil. The mullahs are stalling. Trump isn't blinking. ★★★
Blackburn Goes After Apple

Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) sent a [letter to Apple CEO Tim Cook](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckMHKpDAQhJ9Gb5HYGh0POexlbrPXPUqb7nHCxETSUffxF_cRfmjogqI-ivrzml_og4_rb9zYutPPlGiWY8-8sUtHLvH4spR8bLsUnEHDoDQo0HMMc1uTdTR0ULNtx7EdwOhprD92okUzm0c7jg9oF02o3fQ2D-K3mTpNtbc3SQPc1xvTGMC27_qhI4eDnkzV62MnLCyNS1E4n1j8yT7GdKsUG5e2OthPKbtU3a8KnhU8r-tq3ulv5OuObRU8NyaP98csH1RLQPddjhyVcCRRgUvhrHDfAyvHSQnz18dVYZSLs6gbdduiMARemdTiUepsab98CF6Gser1uqEP_xuVH4x4WvgXAAD__8REhSg) demanding answers about the alleged suppression of conservative content on Apple News -- an app pre-installed on every iPhone. "Apple News has systematically suppressed news articles from conservative publications while amplifying articles from liberal outlets," Blackburn wrote. A Media Research Center study found zero stories from right-leaning outlets in 620 January articles. Powering the app is a [former New York Magazine editor](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycULuunTAQ_BrojMwC5lC4SEN306ZEe-y9sDp-yTZwPz8inxBpipHmodH8-dq-kB2H_Td60ubizUa7lTNl8mTimWs4P1RqPn0qFTeQoIQEAXILbutbq41VA7Sk-3nuFUxymdtDLy9l4P2al-HVg-oNgcFvlGacBlDDSC3rp0kCPBinqZsA-3EY1WANKrlMzSjPZLFS6UwMhfKFlS_iEOLDYuhM9K3TR62pNMOvBtYG1vu-u-_4E-h-Yr6B1ZNlbGBF52gnK96MRWBKjsTjEvQjHL8poxMed0GWa8yiYvmQFQcGm9h8RKkxMxXh2TmOoQhORwwkzkK5tFnbdD9KUXMzyt0ju3_z6n88emn4GwAA___6_ImR) who handpicks stories for hundreds of millions of users. The FTC has already flagged possible [violations of the FTC Act](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDHOpDAMhU8DXVBwIIgixTZ0s-2WyCRmxtqQRCTAHn-VOcIvufgK-5Pf-_NaX8iew_s3HmTszauLbs1XOukgG6-zhOsv5XJeR8oFV5CghQQBcg1-7VtnrNMKWjL9NPUaRjlP7ceAmtU-76A2wn3W_bRtE6LVUs0wocKWTTVJgDrDOHYjYD-oQStnUct5bAZ5JYeFcmdjyHTeWPgmDiFWiqGz8Wi9-ZSScqN-NbA0sDzP0-3xX6Cnnh0NLAc5xgaWbwKxFysyBZeFp1LoFJiSJxHvit7Tm5xI0XNhi15sjFlwyaL66mp7Gpce9p6znppBvg9k_32k_KC728D_AAAA___8KYGd). Congress is done looking the other way.

State of Union: Four Days Out

Trump's first official State of the Union address of his second term [arrives Tuesday, Feb. 24](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLFuxCAQRL8Gd1iwBhwXFGncXdqUFgd7Z3Q2WGZtkr-PfJ8QaYst3oxm5vs23VxcYnp-uRWtP-MUcpjKse24os_HTul4YaH9WLdCbgIBhgvgIKa0TLIJ1gfTQYNW9r00oMXQN7MVUiop5DB4qX0n4XH36m5CuOsBHqEPTbSXkwC4TmndanBSdcp0wTsjBs2UOLbgCEvrcyq4n47iiTGlfH05tT6vzWJnoq2w7pPByGCstbbVlTmmJ-WEP26NCfcLZTAmrOVi5kjI53wUZDAqZaT-UAxGPHH_pUvKKfNXypW_2xZyhDw_OM3IjxRzYjA2uw1bjcsSi-mZEs_VxeUdif6x4mnhLwAA__-21YJX), at 9 p.m. ET. GOP senators are urging an aspirational tone -- address affordability, project strength, and skip the 2024 victory lap. Midterms are on the line.

★★★

**Peter, I’ve learned firsthand that you don’t win elections and govern well alone.** At every step of the way, I’ve been graced with the help and support of countless people who share our values, our passion, and our determination to make this country better. I’ve been overwhelmed by the support for our campaign for U.S. Senate. Already, thousands of people in North Carolina and across this country are standing up to join our fight. I’m hoping to count you among them right now. _As we journey through the most competitive Senate campaign of 2026, I truly need you on our team._ **[Could you make a donation to our campaign today to help us take on the GOP and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5820?t=7&akid=615%2E124072%2EsklOON)** North Carolina is one of the last true purple states in the nation. I won my elections for governor in 2016 and 2020 — and Donald Trump carried the state in the same years. name: Katrina Eames, API PA
subject: Free Subu
body:
https://www.apipennsylvania.org/ [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/]
Hi Peter,
[https://secure.ngpvan.com/X9Rdbs73w0-nDHaXW5e6Og2?contactdata=NX1kFFluPY2UqGsZiQedyxg9SCDsa5ts0T87WHqA/vCpXHmekl4OkALr4VMjXnAmByt2yQkOrfQToPoRaRVLIugzVcHo+JyvHF+8rNdnKeCFHKmZi8hsKZqGmmHeuAbcuO0A678Wpoxyql/E/w7h1K0kAX9ADodkwu4OHymjW6Q=]
We are outraged that Subu Vedam has been denied release on bond and will remain in ICE custody [https://www.statecollege.com/articles/local-news/subu-vedam-denied-release-on-bond-from-ice-custody/] . After being wrongfully imprisoned for over 40 years, his case was overturned but he is still being kept from his family and is now being detained at Moshannon Valley Processing Center. This is wrong, unjust, and cruel. It is a failure of our justice system, but it is more importantly a moral failure. This is another example of how immigrant lives are being treated as disposable.
Keeping Subu detained doesn’t serve any purpose except to further harm him, his family, and our community. This is just proof of how inhumane our immigration system is and how it was designed to hurt people.
Subu should be free. Our communities need an immigration and justice system that is rooted in humanity and dignity, not just endless detention and delay. We need due process that accounts for the fact that our system can fail people - as it has failed the Vedam family over and over again - and seeks to make amends. We invite you to support Subu and his family by learning about his case at freesubu.org [http://freesubu.org] and sign up for their mailing list.
Stay informed, spread the word, and get ready to take action.
[https://secure.ngpvan.com/X9Rdbs73w0-nDHaXW5e6Og2?contactdata=NX1kFFluPY2UqGsZiQedyxg9SCDsa5ts0T87WHqA/vCpXHmekl4OkALr4VMjXnAmByt2yQkOrfQToPoRaRVLIugzVcHo+JyvHF+8rNdnKeCFHKmZi8hsKZqGmmHeuAbcuO0A678Wpoxyql/E/w7h1K0kAX9ADodkwu4OHymjW6Q=]
Katrina Eames

name: Senator Jennifer Boysko
subject: Boysko Bulletin: Week Six Report From Richmond
body:
| | |
---
**Boysko Bulletin: Week Six Report From Richmond**
---
Dear Peter, Crossover marked the deadline for legislation to pass out of its chamber of origin and advance to the other body for consideration. It is both a moment to reflect on the progress we’ve made and to refocus on the work still ahead. Nineteen of my bills passed to the House of Delegates. On Wednesday, the Senate began hearing House bills. I am proud to share several important accomplishments from the first half of the session. My bill, SB 449, has been signed by the Governor, ensuring that this November Virginians will have the opportunity to vote on a constitutional amendment protecting reproductive freedom in the Commonwealth. This represents a significant step forward in safeguarding fundamental rights and empowering the people of Virginia to make their voices heard at the ballot box. SB2, my paid family and medical leave bill, has passed the Senate. The bill will provide up to 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave at 80% of salary/wages, capped at 100% of the average Virginia state weekly wage and employees are promised their jobs back after leave. The program is funded by small contributions from employers and employees. Every individual, from the janitor to the executive, needs time to care for themselves or a loved one when there is a serious illness - like cancer, when they welcome a baby into their family, when a loved one is deployed. No one should be exempt. We are humans first, and all people deserve that dignity. The Senate also passed my legislation strengthening protections under the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, promoting fairness, clarity, and accountability in landlord-tenant relationships across our Commonwealth. As we move into the second half of the session, I remain committed to delivering thoughtful, results-driven policy that reflects the values and priorities of our community. I am fully aware of SB 756, the Fairfax Casino proposal, and I continue to be guided by the voices of my constituents. It has been made abundantly clear that our community does not want or need a casino in Fairfax, and I stand firmly with them. On February 12, I joined the No Casino Coalition for a press conference as they continue organizing, raising awareness, and building momentum to protect the character and future of our community. I spoke in strong opposition on the Senate floor when it was being considered on Friday, Feb. 13th, and unfortunately, it passed and will next be considered in the House. Keep up the important work, continue raising your voices, and remain engaged as we navigate a time when many feel unheard or overlooked. Senate Committee assignments were changed today in the wake of Senator Ebbin moving on to lead the Cannabis Authority. I am pleased to announce that I will be joining the Labor and Commerce Committee. Many of the issues heard in Labor and Commerce affect working families in Virginia. My priorities have long included working to ensure that all Virginians have the opportunity to succeed if they work hard. We must also understand that family friendly policies, including paid sick leave, paid family and medical leave, and fair wages are business friendly, worker retention programs. There are many people suffering in our midst. Be kind. Be compassionate. If you or a loved one are experiencing a mental health crisis, please ask for help. You or a loved one can call the Suicide Crisis Helpline by dialing 988. Our democracy is strongest when communities stay informed, involved, and united. Together, we will continue standing up for our values and fighting for the future our community deserves. Kindest regards,
---
---
Jennifer B. BoyskoMember, Senate of VirginiaRepresenting the 38th Senate District making up the northernmost portions of Fairfax County (Great Falls, Herndon, McLean, Reston, WolfTrap, parts of unincorporated Vienna and a slice of Falls Church) **Photo Gallery**

clean_body: | | | Boysko Bulletin: Week Six Report From Richmond Dear Peter, Crossover marked the deadline for legislation to pass out of its chamber of origin and advance to the other body for consideration. It is both a moment to reflect on the progress we’ve made and to refocus on the work still ahead. Nineteen of my bills passed to the House of Delegates. On Wednesday, the Senate began hearing House bills. I am proud to share several important accomplishments from the first half of the session. My bill, SB 449, has been signed by the Governor, ensuring that this November Virginians will have the opportunity to vote on a constitutional amendment protecting reproductive freedom in the Commonwealth. This represents a significant step forward in safeguarding fundamental rights and empowering the people of Virginia to make their voices heard at the ballot box. SB2, my paid family and medical leave bill, has passed the Senate. The bill will provide up to 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave at 80% of salary/wages, capped at 100% of the average Virginia state weekly wage and employees are promised their jobs back after leave. The program is funded by small contributions from employers and employees. Every individual, from the janitor to the executive, needs time to care for themselves or a loved one when there is a serious illness - like cancer, when they welcome a baby into their family, when a loved one is deployed. No one should be exempt. We are humans first, and all people deserve that dignity. The Senate also passed my legislation strengthening protections under the Virginia Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, promoting fairness, clarity, and accountability in landlord-tenant relationships across our Commonwealth. As we move into the second half of the session, I remain committed to delivering thoughtful, results-driven policy that reflects the values and priorities of our community. I am fully aware of SB 756, the Fairfax Casino proposal, and I continue to be guided by the voices of my constituents. It has been made abundantly clear that our community does not want or need a casino in Fairfax, and I stand firmly with them. On February 12, I joined the No Casino Coalition for a press conference as they continue organizing, raising awareness, and building momentum to protect the character and future of our community. I spoke in strong opposition on the Senate floor when it was being considered on Friday, Feb. 13th, and unfortunately, it passed and will next be considered in the House. Keep up the important work, continue raising your voices, and remain engaged as we navigate a time when many feel unheard or overlooked. Senate Committee assignments were changed today in the wake of Senator Ebbin moving on to lead the Cannabis Authority. I am pleased to announce that I will be joining the Labor and Commerce Committee. Many of the issues heard in Labor and Commerce affect working families in Virginia. My priorities have long included working to ensure that all Virginians have the opportunity to succeed if they work hard. We must also understand that family friendly policies, including paid sick leave, paid family and medical leave, and fair wages are business friendly, worker retention programs. There are many people suffering in our midst. Be kind. Be compassionate. If you or a loved one are experiencing a mental health crisis, please ask for help. You or a loved one can call the Suicide Crisis Helpline by dialing 988. Our democracy is strongest when communities stay informed, involved, and united. Together, we will continue standing up for our values and fighting for the future our community deserves. Kindest regards, Jennifer B. This bill will allow renters to tell judges about the serious defects in their rental homes to defend nonpayment of rent. Defects like a broken stove or refrigerator require renters to spend more on food, leaving less money available for rent, especially for those living pay check to pay check. Senator Boysko's SB 348 passed the Senate and will be heard on the House floor next week. name: Jon Ossoff
subject: Trump talking smack
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
#

_Peter — I’m writing from the campaign trail in Middle Georgia..._
Yesterday, Donald Trump came to Georgia.
The White House sent him here to do damage control on tariffs and health care.
But he just couldn’t help himself: instead of trying to defend his price-inflating tariffs and insurance-premium-doubling health care policy, he resorted to repeating conspiracy theories about the 2020 election — an election he lost in Georgia despite pressuring Georgia election officials to “find” him more votes.
Maybe he’s been watching the rallies I’ve been holding across Georgia, where thousands have turned out in opposition to his corruption and depravity. Because he took a moment to throw some insults my way.
Now, Donald Trump has been insulting me for a long time. But yesterday, it didn’t seem like his heart was in it. I think you could see in his eyes and hear in his voice that he knows he’s lost the American people. That he knows his Presidency is slipping away. That he can feel Georgians, and people nationwide, preparing to deliver a decisive rebuke of historic abuses of power.
Because as I travel across Georgia, what I hear is more and more people of every background and belief reject Trump’s chaos and corruption. And it's not just Democrats and independents. It’s Republicans too!
More and more Republicans take me aside, or they call me on the phone. They tell me they don’t like where this President has taken us. And they tell me they’re going to support a Democrat for the first time.
But here’s the thing: as he gets more desperate, his abuses become more dangerous. From sending Tulsi Gabbard on ballot raids in Fulton County, Georgia, to threatening a national takeover of elections, we have to be ready for anything.
We have to turn out LANDSLIDE margins of victory ... victories so decisive that no scheme or plot hatched in the White House can foil the will of the people.
And we have to defend voting rights with unprecedented tenacity and resources.
**I need your help to do these things.**
[**If you’re able to, please rush $5 right now to my re-election campaign for U.S. Senate. Most people donate $30 but any amount is a big help.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-feb26.GJoCgS&refcode=em260220-1-f&t=1&akid=1697%2E5691347%2ESARTNC)
**[DONATE NOW](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-feb26.GJoCgS&refcode=em260220-1-f&t=2&akid=1697%2E5691347%2ESARTNC)**
Remember — in 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat here couldn’t be done. We built the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history, and we won. That victory secured the Senate majority.
Now we must win again. We will win again.
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
Thanks for your help with this,
Jon

But It Might Be the First Brick in a Digital ID State.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2114823&post_id=188665425&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4NjY1NDI1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzE2MjY3OTIsImV4cCI6MTc3NDIxODc5MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIxMTQ4MjMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.NxLAp0L7G5RRJ1uOBCwcbhQ-ySltHLiPhZ7yGuD1N6E)

**Questions I asked myself early this morning:**
1. Idaho's considering AI chatbot safety laws now?
2. Why can't mom and dad tell their kid to just put the damn phone down?
3. Do we really need the state legislature defining what a chatbot is allowed to say to your 14-year-old?

I'm talking about a bill that passed out of committee this morning and is on its way to the floor: [Senate Bill 1297](https://substack.com/redirect/54e63617-0679-4b1a-b1da-77a89b082fc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/32a430fc-8c7e-413b-9d6f-961c45c164e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Basically, it says that AI chatbots have to tell kids they're not human, refer them to suicide hotlines, and stop simulating romantic relationships with minors.
_Noble enough on paper, right?_
But the bill never requires anyone to verify who's actually a minor, the penalties are a rounding error for companies worth hundreds of billions, and the platforms genuinely wrecking kids' mental health aren't meaningfully covered anyway.
The bill is so vague that "reasonable measures" just means whatever the AI operator _feels like doing_ until someone sues them (which only the AG can do, by the way, so good luck with that timeline).
_**The part that actually should scare you though is that the second you build infrastructure to verify minors online, you've built infrastructure to verify everyone.**_ **So before this passes, someone should answer: where exactly does this stop?**
That's not a slippery slope argument, that's [Australia right now](https://substack.com/redirect/ae0acee5-a1d7-432d-8d47-70ce3ef0924f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
They sold it as "protecting kids." What they actually built was a nationwide biometric ID system where adults hand over face scans to watch cat videos.
So now, Idaho wants to go that direction too?
All for a chatbot bill with $500k penalties that billion-dollar companies will gladly pay without blinking, while covering platforms that aren't even the ones destroying your kid's mental health?
Instagram's still on the phone. Snapchat's still sending streaks at midnight. TikTok's algorithm still knows your daughter better than you do. But sure. Let's regulate whether a chatbot admits it's not human.
**Be the parent.**
**That was always the answer.**

Our private Social Security records need to be just that: Private. Not fodder for the opponents of voting rights at DOGE to pass along to voter suppression groups.
Please, Team, send a letter today to demand Congress investigate DOGE, protect the fundamental right to vote, and defend our data privacy >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/tell-congress-investigate-doges-attempt-to-undermine-our-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks,
Elon Musk’s DOGE took millions of Americans’ private Social Security records and handed access to election deniers . Congress needs to make sure it never happens again.
The Department of Justice has now admitted that the Department of Government Efficiency gained sweeping access to addresses, birthdates, and identifiers that can be weaponized to target voters, suppress turnout, or erode trust in elections. DOGE’s access came as Trump and his allies escalated attacks on mail-in voting and independent federal agencies.
That context matters. This was a power grab designed to undermine our democracy using our private data. Congress must not ignore this or look away.
Tell Congress to investigate DOGE’s efforts to access and share our private Social Security data with election deniers. Demand that all who participated in the scheme are held accountable, and make sure this never happens again >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/tell-congress-investigate-doges-attempt-to-undermine-our-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]

DOGE was created by executive order, shielded from transparency, and staffed with political loyalists. Reports show its operatives bypassed standard clearance procedures and ignored internal warnings to gain and share “unprecedented” access to our data with no guardrails.
DOGE staffers engaged in prohibited political activity while embedded inside a nonpartisan agency in violation of the Hatch Act. This is how elections are undermined from inside the government.
Congress must act now — not only to expose what happened, but to ensure it can never happen again . The House Oversight Committee and the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee must launch a full investigation, subpoena DOGE leadership, and lock in safeguards so no future administration can abuse federal data to rig the system.

Congress must act now — not only to expose what happened, but to ensure it can never happen again . The House Oversight Committee and the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee must launch a full investigation, subpoena DOGE leadership, and lock in safeguards so no future administration can abuse federal data to rig the system. | | _“Much weaker than I suspected."_ _“I can’t figure out how this got through any proper review.”_ _“Rehashed conspiracy theories and debunked lies.”_ Imagine turning in a paper and getting that feedback from your teacher. Well, those are just a few of the expert reactions to a recently unsealed FBI search warrant affidavit — which relied on disproven claims to try to justify their raid on an elections office in Georgia’s largest county. Take a look: **“It’s hard to see how the contents of this affidavit rise to the level of probable cause.”** —Joyce Vance, former U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama “I didn’t see anything in my first read of this about the sources’ credibility — their views of the election, anything that would suggest bias, motive, inaccuracies — and that’s exactly what you have to put in...I just don’t know that I can think of another warrant where I’ve not seen such information about the sources of information included. **That’s not normal, especially in something this high profile.** ” —Andrew Weissmann, former General Counsel for the FBI, Chief of the Criminal Fraud Section of the DOJ, and Assistant United States Attorney “The basis for the FBI raid in Fulton County appears to be **a lot of previously disproven allegations.** ” —Miles Taylor, former national security official And here’s what it all comes down to: **“Why are they doing this? Because Trump wants to get his hands on our votes. He said Republicans should run elections. This is a power grab, creating a pretense to interfere in the 2026 elections.”** —Lauren Groh-Wargo, CEO, Fair Fight In the raid, Trump’s FBI seized hundreds of boxes of ballots and records from 2020, which they could use to try to justify a takeover of local election administration by Georgia’s MAGA-aligned State Election Board — just in time for the midterms. MAGA’s intentions are clear: silence the will of the people. But we are not backing down. We’ll continue to track and expose the far right’s lies about elections, we’ll continue to push back against their voter suppression attempts, and we’ll continue helping to elect leaders who respect and protect the freedom to vote in free and fair elections. Thank you for everything you do to make this work possible. In solidarity, The Fair Fight Team

### _" Deport Every Indian"_
That's what a sitting Republican elected official proudly said, along with other hateful, racist remarks.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a3f0da9b-4966-4445-ae61-904049716273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My name is Raja _(RAH-JUH, in case you find a four-letter name hard to pronounce like Mr. Langevin)_ , and I'm an immigrant.**I 'm also a proud American, and I'm running to serve my state of Illinois in the U.S. Senate.**
But dangerous attacks like the one above are setting a dangerous precedent for Indian Americans - and frankly, all people of color.
**Their words carry weight.** And while I've become used to the hate speech, the ridiculous calls for mass deportation of Indian Americans, and the outright racial profiling, I'm doing everything in my power to change that reality for my children - and the next generation.
Because let's be clear: When folks use cruel tactics and racial profiling like this, they're not just coming after me - they're coming after anyone who doesn't fit their narrow definition of what an American looks like.
I'm a proud citizen of the United States, but because of the rhetoric coming straight from Donald Trump and the far-right movement, people are questioning whether I belong in this country or on the floor of the U.S. Senate.
_This isn 't just politics. This is personal._
**[If you agree that hate has no place here and want to build a future where Americans aren't judged for their skin color or the sound of their name, I'm hoping I can count on your support right now.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a3f0da9b-4966-4445-ae61-904049716273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW ➔](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a3f0da9b-4966-4445-ae61-904049716273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My family came to this country when I was three months old, chasing the American Dream. The Illinois community gave me a chance. Public schools gave me an education. This country gave my family hope.
So here's what these small-minded individuals don't understand: _**I love this country enough to fight like hell for it.**_
That's exactly what I've been doing.
I've spent every single day taking on the racist bullies in charge. I stood up to Kristi Noem when she tried to dodge accountability for the treatment of immigrants. I had the police called on me for trying to inspect ICE facilities. I've called out Trump's illegal ICE raids and his attacks on immigrant communities.
I drove cross-country to cast my vote against Trump's agenda. I've questioned his officials in hearings, condemned his illegal tariffs, and introduced legislation to repeal his devastating cuts to SNAP and Medicaid.
I refuse to back down. I refuse to be intimidated. And I refuse to let hate win.
### **That 's why I'm running for Senate.**
Right now, we need leaders who will rise up to meet the threat of the MAGA movement head-on. Leaders who know that any attack on any community is an attack on us all.
**Here 's the deal**: the 2026 midterms are our chance to take back the House, flip the Senate, and end Trump's unchecked power. The only thing standing between us and a blue wave? A $300 million warchest dedicated to defeating Democrats like me.
There's no doubt in my mind, they'll use every dollar to prop up the same racist extremists who are attacking me right now.
The only way we fight back is together - with a massive grassroots movement of people who believe that hate has no place in American politics.
**So I 'm asking you directly: Are you ready to fight like hell with me?**
If you want leaders who refuse to be scared away by hateful words - who'll stand up for every American, no matter what their name sounds like or where they came from - I need you in this fight with me.
**[Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can to help me win this Senate race and turn the page on this dark moment in our country?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a3f0da9b-4966-4445-ae61-904049716273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE NOW ➔](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a3f0da9b-4966-4445-ae61-904049716273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm a proud American citizen. And I'm not going anywhere.
Thank you for standing with me,
Raja Krishnamoorthi

# **Dems made a bad bill better this week**
---
| |
| | | | | **Director's Report - Week 6 of the 2026 Legislative Session from the Desk of Nick Sotille SC House Democratic Caucus**
---
| **Run for State House!** We have just over a month until candidate filing opens and the [**South Carolina Democratic Party**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=88c08b0436&e=edbde6c9b1) is looking for Democrats to run up and down the ballot.

**House Democrats make a bad bill better.** [**H. 4757**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=62b4d9bcf3&e=edbde6c9b1) , the "Parental Rights" bill came to the floor this week and [**Rep. Courtney Waters (D-Charleston)**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=c1ca818480&e=edbde6c9b1) , [**Rep. Wendell Jones (D-Greenville)**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=551226d7cc&e=edbde6c9b1) , and [**Rep. Spencer Wetmore (D-Charleston)**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a0026fb6ab&e=edbde6c9b1) led the charge, sponsoring amendments to change key provisions in the bill. The amendments aimed to protect victims of child abuse and neglect, limit legal liability under the bill, and allow parents to opt-in to give doctors the authority to provide care to their children without getting parental permission first. And guess what? It worked. Four of our amendments were adopted, with bipartisan support - over opposition from the far right "Freedom" Caucus.

**Jordan Pace leads Republicans to new lows.** Jordan Pace introduces a bill the gerrymander Congressman James E. Clyburn’s District. Our state's Congressional map is already ridiculously gerrymandered - Democrats typically garner over 40% of the statewide vote, but hold just 14% of the state's Congressional seats.
The Jordanmander bill, [**H. 4717**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=04078ecbfc&e=edbde6c9b1) , will get a subcommittee hearing on Wednesday at 9:00am.
---
|
---
| | | | | |

# **Contact your State House Rep & Rep Travis Moore and demand they vote no on ICE Collaboration Bill**
---
| |

[**House Bill 4764**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=099ab47147&e=edbde6c9b1) would require every agency that operates a correctional facility to enter a written collaboration agreement with ICE through its 287(g) program. The House AI, Cybersecurity & Special Laws Subcommittee heard testimony Tuesday afternoon from 22 South Carolinians who signed up to speak. _Every speaker opposed H. 4764._ Additionally, at least 125 South Carolinians have sent written messages to their lawmakers opposing the bill using the form at [**aclusc.org/iceout**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=6a90030e11&e=edbde6c9b1)

During a two-hour public hearing on Tuesday, Feb. 17, every public testifier voiced strong opposition to a bill that would force local law enforcement agencies to sign collaboration agreements with U.S. Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE).The subcommittee did not take a vote on Tuesday. Rep. Travis Moore (R-Spartanburg), who chairs the subcommittee and sponsored the bill, said the subcommittee will vote at a subsequent meeting. No meeting date has been announced yet. [**Learn More**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=dae8d8a224&e=edbde6c9b1)

| |
These past couple of weeks we hosted our third installment of A Candid Conversation Series at Wofford with the Honorable Judge Sherrie Lydon and Adair Ford Boroughs discussing the rule of law. I also got to witness my friend Councilwoman Erica Brown’s swearing in for her fourth term on City Council.
We showed up for the People’s Day Protest on President’s Day in full force. Thanks to the United Stakeholders for Democracy who keep showing up every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month to rally on the corner of St. Johns and Church St. at noon. Last night I stopped by the Charleston Democrats monthly meeting to support my friend Rep Spencer Wetmore and we had a surprise visit from Gubernatorial Candidate Rep Jermaine Johnson!
Stay with me y’all, democracy is a participatory sport.

## **South Korea And The UK Act Democratically; The U.S. Like A Failing State**
Yesterday, **South Korea** sentenced its former president to life in prison for his attempt to declare martial law. Not exile. Not house arrest. Prison. (They even debated _the death penalty,_ a sentence not imposed since December, 1997).
Ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol will spend from here to eternity in the pokey for masterminding an insurrection. Per the Seoul court, on December 3rd, 2024, Yoon attempted to subvert South Korea's constitution, deploying troops to seal off the National Assembly and ordering the arrest of rival politicians, the press and activists.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25324cf9-c3d7-4b86-b2d8-0fd88767a240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That is what those living in democracies call a "no-no."
Judge Ji Gwi-yeon determined _Yoon 's actions fundamentally damaged South Korea's democracy_. You can be sure there was no offer to do his time in a Ghislaine Maxwell country club prison. Or a Donald Trump...well, nothing, because former Attorney General Merrick Garland was apparently catching up on _Days of our Lives_ episodes instead of doing his fucking job the first 18 months of his term as AG.

But Romania, as an actual democracy, acted with the urgency to protect their constitutional system you'd think all countries would exhibit in response to an existential threat.
From PBS:
> Romania's constitutional court threw out the results of the election's first round and delayed the second round. The sitting government says there was a vast influence effort by a foreign actor to boost the candidacy of a candidate dubbed as pro-Russian, anti-NATO and anti-semitic.
Does that second part sound familiar to anyone? Yet, Romania went further, barring the pro-Putin candidate from the run-off ballot.

That sadistic lug was found guilty by military tribunal of genocide, subverting state power, destruction of public assets, and undermining the national economy.
Here I was, a decade and a half later, lecturing at Romanian universities, speaking on televised news programs, and meeting with diplomats, professors, press, politicians, and students at top universities. All under the auspices of discussing how Romania could continue its move toward more liberal democracy.
**Uh-huh. Apparently we should 've brought a Romanian politician or scholar into my home state of Ohio **_**to explain how democracy works to us**_**.**
The United States--the nation that invented modern constitutional checks and balances--had four years to try, likely jail, and eliminate the threat to our democracy posed by Donald Trump, once President Joe Biden won in 2020 (_full disclosure:_ I wrote ads for then Vice-President Biden in that race).
Four. Fucking. Years.
But Garland--his attorney general choice, and one by all accounts he enormously regretted making--was the worst attorney general _not_ in U.S. history, but galactic history. Garland gave the Supreme Court all the time in the world to deliver its wholly ahistorical--and full of more shit than a dog park on top of a horse barn on top of Donald Trump's diaper at the end of a Taco Trump day--decision that the President is...well, a king. If irony were electricity, the Founders would be spinning in their graves fast enough to power the Eastern Seaboard.

## The Constitution Is Not a Branding Exercise
Our founding document inspired democracies across the globe. The separation of powers. Checks and balances. No kings. No untouchables. Other countries adopted those ideas, values, laws, and--here's the wild part--they actually still enforce them!
In America, the Constitution has now been rendered a campaign prop, like an *assassin in Butler, PA. The Constitution's something to wave around at rallies before the Jabba-esque jabroni stuffs it back in his pocket alongside to grievance politics, donor checks, and some week-old KFC chicken wings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25324cf9-c3d7-4b86-b2d8-0fd88767a240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

**The real difference between us, South Korea and the UK right now isn 't legal structure. It's political will. The latter two were willing to prosecute power.**
We're terrified of it.

## Democrats: Learn the Lesson or Lose the Country
This is where the rubber meets the road.
Democrats cannot continue behaving like the adult in the room politely asking the arsonist to stop setting fires. While complimenting the arsonist on his/her nice shoes.
Other democracies understand something we used to get, yet since Gerald Ford's ill-considered pardon of Richard Nixon, Iran-Contra, and Iraq-gate. **If you do not enforce accountability, you incentivize escalation.**
There are a host of pro-reality, pro-liberal policy, take-no-crap Democrats currently growing in stature--Reps. Dan Goldman, Eric Swalwell, Melanie Stansbury, Lucy McBath, AOC, and Ted Lieu, to name a few. Not to mention Sens. Chris Murphy, Tammy Duckworth, Elizabeth Warren, Adam Schiff, and Ruben Gallego.
There are more.
They must take the reigns of power if we're to survive this moment, _as soon as humanly possible_. South Korea didn't say, "Well, let's not prosecute the fascist, Yoon. I mean, we don't want to divide the country!" Britain didn't say, "Let's move on for the sake of unity."
They said: if you break the law at the highest levels, you face consequences at the highest levels. Don't pass go. Hit the brakes. Slow your roll. Because it's time to go habitate in the Big House, treacherous scum.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25324cf9-c3d7-4b86-b2d8-0fd88767a240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Democrats need to internalize this--deeply. Voters are not energized by procedural scolding. Or charts with a fetchingly colorful X and Y axis about how things get better when they're in power.
Voters are energized by strength. By clarity. By authentic anger. By visible consequences. Accountability is not "political."And it most certainly isn't "partisan." **It 's oxygen for democracy.**
Right now, the United States looks bloated, feeble, flaccid, and corrupted, much like it's President. A nation captured by billionaire predators who've preyed on young girls, your pension, programs like SNAP, USAID, or Medicaid, weaponized social media against you, rejected your healthcare claims on a technicality...
I could go on. And on.
They are beyond-gilded age parasites with a dangerous amount of money and power in a democracy. Every Democrat must target them, purposely become their enemy. They already see you that way.
There's no playing paddy cake with these people. There's only (rhetorically, politically and with massive regulations) punching them in the mouth. Procedural cowardice, and an addiction to treating authoritarian behavior as "just politics" won't get us out of this. This doubly goes for you, Don Bacon, Brian Fitzpatrick, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis...you _reasonable_(see: cowering) Republicans who give quisling a bad name.
Folks, we lecture the world about democracy while struggling to enforce it at home. What an absolute joke. We used to export rule of law. Now we export dysfunction. And yes--the world sees it.
Democracies modeled after ours are functioning more effectively than we are and shaking their heads at the circus going on over here. Wondering what the hell happened to us.
That's not just humiliating. It's dangerous.
The message isn't vengeance. It's stability.
The message isn't partisanship. It's constitutional order.
The American public understands fairness. They understand consequences. **What they don 't understand is why it only applies to them.**
The principles are as simple as they were when we wrote them (even if we too often didn't live up to them): No one is above the law--no one. Not kings. Not princes. Not presidents.
History does not reward timidity. It does not remember the cautious caretakers of decline. It remembers those who defended the system when it mattered. You either continue tiptoeing around authoritarianism, or confront it directly, frame it clearly, and demand consequences loudly.
One path preserves democracy. The other manages its decay.

South Korea imprisoned a president. Britain arrested a prince. America is the O.J. Simpson Trial in applying rule of law | | and | Feb 20 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. by Cliff Schecter South Korea And The UK Act Democratically; The U.S. Like A Failing State Yesterday, South Korea sentenced its former president to life in prison for his attempt to declare martial law. Not exile. Not house arrest. Prison. (They even debated the death penalty, a sentence not imposed since December, 1997). Ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol will spend from here to eternity in the pokey for masterminding an insurrection. Per the Seoul court, on December 3rd, 2024, Yoon attempted to subvert South Korea's constitution, deploying troops to seal off the National Assembly and ordering the arrest of rival politicians, the press and activists. | | ---|---|--- That is what those living in democracies call a "no-no." Judge Ji Gwi-yeon determined Yoon 's actions fundamentally damaged South Korea's democracy. You can be sure there was no offer to do his time in a Ghislaine Maxwell country club prison. Or a Donald Trump...well, nothing, because former Attorney General Merrick Garland was apparently catching up on Days of our Lives episodes instead of doing his fucking job the first 18 months of his term as AG. | | ---|---|--- So, South Korea, a democratic republic that emerged from dictatorship in the late 20th century just proved--in 14 months, l ess time than it took Garland to appoint a special counsel to investigate the most sweeping act of armed sedition in America since the Civil War --that at least to them, the rule of law is not just a slogan. Or a talking point tossed around on cable by the likes of Scott Jennings--who I hear wets himself on set--like feces flung from a monkey. A myth told around campfires about a unique brand of American exceptionalism that never actually existed, and at this point is utterly laughable to apply to our c ity rolling down a hill. In the United Kingdom , there was also justice for predation, and this time it was a member of the Epstein class. Prince Andrew was arrested. A literal royal. In a country that still technically has a monarchy. | | ---|---|--- So let's pause here for a mere moment to take a moral inventory. The monarchy country arrested a prince. The post-authoritarian democracy imprisoned a president. In Brazil, where democracy stretches all the way back to release of Back to the Future in movie theaters, fulminating foreskin Jair Bolsonaro also tried to coup. He was disqualified from running for office again. Then subsequently sentenced to 27 years in prison. In Romania, a presidential candidate came out of nowhere to dominate social media platforms and fundraising, which Romanian intelligence tied to Putin. Kinda like how we tied Trump's rise in 2016 to Putin. But Romania, as an actual democracy, acted with the urgency to protect their constitutional system you'd think all countries would exhibit in response to an existential threat. From PBS: Romania's constitutional court threw out the results of the election's first round and delayed the second round. The sitting government says there was a vast influence effort by a foreign actor to boost the candidacy of a candidate dubbed as pro-Russian, anti-NATO and anti-semitic. Does that second part sound familiar to anyone? Yet, Romania went further, barring the pro-Putin candidate from the run-off ballot. | | ---|---|--- Wanna hear a story? About 20 years ago I was working on democracy promotion for the U.S. State Department, who dispatched me to Romania. This was 15 years post-execution of the tyrannical, Communist dictator Nikolas Ceacescu in Bucharest's public square (bullet holes still marked the walls). That sadistic lug was found guilty by military tribunal of genocide, subverting state power, destruction of public assets, and undermining the national economy. Here I was, a decade and a half later, lecturing at Romanian universities, speaking on televised news programs, and meeting with diplomats, professors, press, politicians, and students at top universities. All under the auspices of discussing how Romania could continue its move toward more liberal democracy. Uh-huh. Apparently we should 've brought a Romanian politician or scholar into my home state of Ohio to explain how democracy works to us. The United States--the nation that invented modern constitutional checks and balances--had four years to try, likely jail, and eliminate the threat to our democracy posed by Donald Trump, once President Joe Biden won in 2020 (full disclosure: I wrote ads for then Vice-President Biden in that race). Four. Fucking. Years. But Garland--his attorney general choice, and one by all accounts he enormously regretted making--was the worst attorney general not in U.S. history, but galactic history. He worried about all the same craptastic garbage our corporate media obsesses with today instead of just doing their GD job--"the appearance of partisanship," "strict adherence to a code" that did not envision a madman like Trump, and an unwillingness to tell the American people what he was doing about January 6th, and why. Garland gave the Supreme Court all the time in the world to deliver its wholly ahistorical--and full of more shit than a dog park on top of a horse barn on top of Donald Trump's diaper at the end of a Taco Trump day--decision that the President is...well, a king. One imagines if Ben Franklin were around, he would've found a way to conduct lightning into the Supreme Court building that day. Essentially, all you need to know is Alito, Roberts, Thomas, Gorsuch, and Barrett would've supported King George in 1776. He had absolute immunity after all! Tax away! Bring more guns to the Boston Massacre next time! If irony were electricity, the Founders would be spinning in their graves fast enough to power the Eastern Seaboard. The Constitution Is Not a Branding Exercise Our founding document inspired democracies across the globe. The separation of powers. Checks and balances. No kings. No untouchables. Other countries adopted those ideas, values, laws, and--here's the wild part--they actually still enforce them! In America, the Constitution has now been rendered a campaign prop, like an assassin in Butler, PA. The Constitution's something to wave around at rallies before the Jabba-esque jabroni stuffs it back in his pocket alongside to grievance politics, donor checks, and some week-old KFC chicken wings. | | ---|---|--- The real difference between us, South Korea and the UK right now isn 't legal structure. It's political will. The latter two were willing to prosecute power. We're terrified of it. Democrats: Learn the Lesson or Lose the Country This is where the rubber meets the road. Democrats cannot continue behaving like the adult in the room politely asking the arsonist to stop setting fires. While complimenting the arsonist on his/her nice shoes. Other democracies understand something we used to get, yet since Gerald Ford's ill-considered pardon of Richard Nixon, Iran-Contra, and Iraq-gate. If you do not enforce accountability, you incentivize escalation. There are a host of pro-reality, pro-liberal policy, take-no-crap Democrats currently growing in stature--Reps. Dan Goldman, Eric Swalwell, Melanie Stansbury, Lucy McBath, AOC, and Ted Lieu, to name a few. Not to mention Sens. Chris Murphy, Tammy Duckworth, Elizabeth Warren, Adam Schiff, and Ruben Gallego. There are more. They must take the reigns of power if we're to survive this moment, as soon as humanly possible. South Korea didn't say, "Well, let's not prosecute the fascist, Yoon. I mean, we don't want to divide the country!" Britain didn't say, "Let's move on for the sake of unity." They said: if you break the law at the highest levels, you face consequences at the highest levels. Don't pass go. Hit the brakes. Slow your roll. Because it's time to go habitate in the Big House, treacherous scum. | | ---|---|--- Democrats need to internalize this--deeply. Voters are not energized by procedural scolding. Or charts with a fetchingly colorful X and Y axis about how things get better when they're in power. Voters are energized by strength. By clarity. By authentic anger. By visible consequences. Accountability is not "political."And it most certainly isn't "partisan." It 's oxygen for democracy. Right now, the United States looks bloated, feeble, flaccid, and corrupted, much like it's President. A nation captured by billionaire predators who've preyed on young girls, your pension, programs like SNAP, USAID, or Medicaid, weaponized social media against you, rejected your healthcare claims on a technicality... I could go on. And on. They are beyond-gilded age parasites with a dangerous amount of money and power in a democracy. Every Democrat must target them, purposely become their enemy. They already see you that way. There's no playing paddy cake with these people. There's only (rhetorically, politically and with massive regulations) punching them in the mouth. Procedural cowardice, and an addiction to treating authoritarian behavior as "just politics" won't get us out of this. This doubly goes for you, Don Bacon, Brian Fitzpatrick, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis...you reasonable(see: cowering) Republicans who give quisling a bad name. Folks, we lecture the world about democracy while struggling to enforce it at home. What an absolute joke. We used to export rule of law. Now we export dysfunction. And yes--the world sees it. Democracies modeled after ours are functioning more effectively than we are and shaking their heads at the circus going on over here. Wondering what the hell happened to us. That's not just humiliating. It's dangerous. The message isn't vengeance. It's stability. The message isn't partisanship. It's constitutional order. The American public understands fairness. They understand consequences. What they don 't understand is why it only applies to them. The principles are as simple as they were when we wrote them (even if we too often didn't live up to them): No one is above the law--no one. Not kings. Not princes. Not presidents. History does not reward timidity. It does not remember the cautious caretakers of decline. It remembers those who defended the system when it mattered. You either continue tiptoeing around authoritarianism, or confront it directly, frame it clearly, and demand consequences loudly. One path preserves democracy. The other manages its decay. Why This Matters -- And Why This Space Matters If you're reading this, you already understand the stakes. But independent platforms like this are the only way we get accountability. Corporate media normalizes lawbreaking and cruelty. Social media algorithms reward outrage and Nazis. Political consultants (I know, I was one) too often default to caution. . allows us to: Keep pushing uncomfortable truths Expand investigative deep dives Hold power accountable consistently Build a community that refuses to normalize corruption Keep adding content. We're one of few media orgs invited to live stream the Counter-SOTU even in Washington, D.C. Tuesday. With speakers such as Robert de Niro, Mark Ruffalo, Joyce Vance, George Conway, and Stacey Abrams. We 'll bring this event right into your living room, making it like you're there.. Democracy requires citizens who refuse to look away. If we're going to demand our leaders function, . Let's build that, my friends. central plank of his economic agenda

In striking down his tariff regime, the Court made one thing clear — the
presidency is not a throne. The American economy is not one of Trump’s
sham side hustles. And he is not a king.

Trump does not see judges as independent guardians of the Constitution. He
sees them as loyalists who owe him something. He handpicked justices like
Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett because he believed
they would protect him — not the law.

But judges are supposed to be loyal to the Constitution, not to Trump’s
ego.

We didn’t win because this Court suddenly found its conscience. We got
lucky. Enough conservative justices were willing, this time, to protect
corporate interests hurt by Trump’s tariffs. That’s what drew the line.
Not a moral awakening.

There is no guarantee we’ll be this “lucky” again.

Trump will feel humiliated by this decision. And humiliation makes him
more dangerous. He will double down on his demands for loyalty. He will
demand judges who bend. Judges who, when he says “jump,” answer “how
high?”

That’s the danger. The Supreme Court is in crisis, and the only way to end
the stranglehold of partisan power brokers who treat lifetime seats like
political trophies is reform.

That kind of pressure doesn’t build itself. It takes organizing. It takes
accountability campaigns. It takes sustained grassroots power. And that’s
exactly what Demand Justice PAC is fighting to build.

The State Party will provide the most important facts - a kernel of truth - from the week. _[If you were forwarded this newsletter, you can sign up to receive the Kernel every week by clicking here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125812121/602978121/1416943042?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzM1MDMwZi1hZjBlLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_Bjfoh4ZeIEq4N33hgBAL7ZuS-mtjNZL2t6sZhn3RqQ=&emci=a53da6f0-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=6335030f-af0e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&ceid=4925535)_ [_**Donate to the INDems' 2026 Ready Fund today.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125812122/602978122/383765187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzM1MDMwZi1hZjBlLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_Bjfoh4ZeIEq4N33hgBAL7ZuS-mtjNZL2t6sZhn3RqQ=) ****
_Republicans Sneak in Language To Cut Early Voting Days in Half_ [__](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125812123/602978123/1937516516?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzM1MDMwZi1hZjBlLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_Bjfoh4ZeIEq4N33hgBAL7ZuS-mtjNZL2t6sZhn3RqQ=&emci=a53da6f0-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=6335030f-af0e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&ceid=4925535) This week, without taking any public testimony whatsoever, the Indiana Senate Elections Committee passed an amendment onto [House Bill 1359](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125812124/602978124/138360965?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzM1MDMwZi1hZjBlLWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_Bjfoh4ZeIEq4N33hgBAL7ZuS-mtjNZL2t6sZhn3RqQ=&emci=a53da6f0-a80e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=6335030f-af0e-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&ceid=4925535) which would cut early voting access down from 28 days to just 16 days – starting as soon as the May 2026 primary. **The full Senate will vote on this bill sometime next week. Call your State Senator at 317-232-9600 and tell them to oppose this attack on early voting.** More and more Hoosiers choose to vote early in each passing general election. # **SCOTUS strikes down Trump 's IEEPA tariffs but leaves $200 billion refund question unanswered**
The Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's sweeping International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariffs on Friday **[but did not address whether the U.S. must refund more than $200 billion already collected.](https://substack.com/redirect/1a4afc61-6ae2-43f7-996b-1a1125984660?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Dissenting Justice Brett Kavanaugh warned "refunds of billions of dollars would have significant consequences for the U.S. Treasury," calling the potential process a "mess" as refunds could be required to foreign nations, consumers, and manufacturers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a4afc61-6ae2-43f7-996b-1a1125984660?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had planned to use the $200 billion in tariff revenue to shrink the $2 trillion deficit and pay down the $36 trillion debt.
* **What 's next:** Trump said at a White House press conference Friday he will continue issuing tariffs under Section 232 authorities rather than relying on IEEPA emergency powers. The ruling could impact Trump's broader use of tariffs as a foreign policy tool -- he recently threatened tariffs on countries doing business with Iran and warned China of increased tariffs if it doesn't ship rare earth minerals to the U.S. Trump argues tariffs are needed to address national security concerns about the "hollowing out of the manufacturing base" and dependence on foreign adversaries.

Hey folks,
I jumped on live with **Don Lemon** to discuss the first real, meaningful rebuke from the Supreme Court smacking down Trump's tariffs. This was a 6-3 ruling that said the president of the United States cannot just invent taxes because he feels like it. And it hit at the heart of Trump's entire economic strategy. We talked about what it means, whether he'll even follow it, and the question nobody in Washington seems eager to answer: where the hell is your money?
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:00:22**] I explain why this ruling is basically a bailout for House and Senate Republicans -- they refused to stop the tariffs themselves, so the Supreme Court did their job for them.
* [**00:01:52**] The core constitutional issue: taxation without representation. Congress levies taxes. Not kings. Not presidents playing emergency theater.
* [**00:02:32**] The question Washington doesn't want to touch -- what happens to the tariff money Americans already paid? Do families get refunds? Or is it just... gone?
* [**00:07:58**] Trump reportedly flies off the handle when he learns about the ruling, raging about courts limiting his power. Because constraints are kind of the whole point.
* [**00:09:36**] The international fallout: Trump built his foreign policy around tariff threats. Now that leverage is gone. What does a weakened, cornered president do next?

We also talked about who actually pays the price when leaders abuse power. About why working families keep getting squeezed while Washington plays games. The average American household paid $1,500-$2,000 more last year because of these tariffs. That's real money. For people living paycheck to paycheck, that's groceries. Rent. Childcare. And now the Court says the tariffs were illegal. This episode isn't just about a legal ruling. It's about whether our institutions still function. Whether Congress will ever do its job. Whether voters will demand better. If you value independent voices willing to say it plainly, help me keep building this.

With urgency,
--Mike

Derek – we wanted to bump John’s email to the top of your inbox.
---
**We need just 11 more responses from 18326 to our new February Priorities Survey, and the deadline is at midnight tonight.**
Your feedback is critical to putting us in the strongest possible position heading into the next month and beyond. **[Please, will you take the survey now?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52922?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=1&akid=10604%2E434096%2EtVOYFu)**
| | [Take the Survey](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52922?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=2&akid=10604%2E434096%2EtVOYFu)
---
Thanks so much,
Team Fetterman
\---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: John Fetterman
Sent: Tuesday, Feb. 17
Subject: I'm looking forward to sitting down and reading your thoughts
| | |
---
Derek, can I get your thoughts? It won't take more than a minute or two.
Now that we're in the full swing of the election year, it's crucial to get your ongoing input on our strategy to win big in the upcoming midterms.
I know you've likely taken one of these surveys before and felt like no one actually read your responses. But I can tell you straight: That won't be the case here.
**I wish more than anything that I could sit down at the kitchen table with every family across PA and listen. But since I can’t, I'll be sitting down at my own kitchen table to read each and every response to this survey.**
**[Will you take this February Priorities Survey now to tell me what you want me to focus on?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52922?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=3&akid=10604%2E434096%2EtVOYFu)**
| | [Take the Survey](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52922?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=4&akid=10604%2E434096%2EtVOYFu)
---
What you share here will help me and my team map out our game plan for the month ahead – and see how we can continue standing up for you and your family.
Thanks for taking the time,

John
| |

name: Heather G.
subject: Republicans are coming after families like mine.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103720?t=6&akid=23065%2E878179%2ERNBpsb) Friend, I’m the Executive Director of the Voter Protection Project and I’m fuming with rage.

**House Republicans just passed The Save America Act—a voter suppression bill that directly attacks families like mine.**

My wife and I met in 2016 working at a Democratic polling firm. We knocked doors together. We worked midterms together. We postponed our wedding when COVID shut the world down.

When we finally got married in 2022, we combined our last names — something our friends had joked about for years. It felt joyful. It felt like building a life together.

Like millions of married women in this country, that means our birth certificates no longer match our legal names.

We’re lucky. We both have updated passports with our new last name.

**But unfortunately, a lot of Americans don’t.**

The SAVE Act would create new documentation requirements that could turn something as common as a name change into a barrier to registering and voting.

Noncitizen voting is already illegal and exceedingly rare.

This bill doesn’t solve a real problem. It tells us exactly who Republicans don’t want at the ballot box. And that’s why we’re fighting back.

[The Voter Protection Project works every day to protect voters and elect Democrats who will defend the freedom to vote — not restrict it. If you believe the right to vote should never depend on whether your paperwork is perfectly aligned, will you chip in today? »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103720?t=7&akid=23065%2E878179%2ERNBpsb) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/103721?t=8&akid=23065%2E878179%2ERNBpsb)

Every dollar you give helps us flip the House and Senate by electing voting rights champions who will fight back against Republican voter suppression.

This fight isn’t theoretical.

**It’s about ensuring families like mine — and families like yours — can participate in our democracy without jumping through unnecessary hoops.**

We’re not backing down.

In solidarity,

Heather G.
Executive Director
The Voter Protection Project

body:
Trump has deployed two carrier groups to the region — that’s around 10,000 sailors, two aircraft carriers, about a dozen destroyers and cruisers, and 150 or more of the world's most advanced fighters and attack aircraft.
#
Peter, we don’t know how this isn’t the only thing anyone is talking about, but Trump wants to attack Iran in the next week and a half.
He’s virtually admitted it, in public! Trump has deployed two carrier groups to the region — that’s around 10,000 sailors, two aircraft carriers, about a dozen destroyers and cruisers, and 150 or more of the world's most advanced fighters and attack aircraft.
Our allies are taking this seriously, with the UK preventing him from using bases on their soil to strike Iran. Iran is taking this seriously by fortifying their nuclear and military sites, shifting their forces, and preparing retaliatory strike lists. Every expert you can ask will tell you the threat is very real.
He wants to strike Iran to look tough, and Rubio and Hegseth are on board because they’ve never met a war they didn’t like. One problem: This war is a choice. There is no strategic imperative, no significant threat that has to be hit to defend our people or our troops. If there was, they already would’ve done it.
They are choosing to do this, and the only way to stop them is by demanding action from Congress. There are Democratic sponsored War Powers Resolutions in both the House and Senate that would get the job done. They need to come up for a vote, and if they do they’re probably going to pass.
But the only way we get that done is by raising hell.
[**We’re counting on you here. Please, add your name and demand that Congress do its job and stop Trump and the GOP from plunging the United States into another war of choice that nobody wants.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/260220_VV_EM_IRAN/?refcode=em260220-1-MK&t=1&akid=34956%2E3013755%2E5W8qHl)
